definition: Document clustering (or text clustering) is the application of cluster analysis to textual documents.
details: It has applications in automatic document organization, topic extraction and fast information retrieval or filtering.

explainer.lead: Document clustering uses cluster analysis to place textual documents into groups. Those groups can help organize collections, extract topics, and make information retrieval or filtering faster.

tiers.eli5: Imagine asking a computer to sort a big pile of writings into smaller piles. Each smaller pile contains documents grouped by cluster analysis, making the collection easier to organize or search.
tiers.practitioner: Apply cluster analysis to a textual document collection, then use the resulting document groups for organization, topic extraction, retrieval, or filtering. The groups are an intermediate result: topic extraction and retrieval or filtering are applications built on them, not automatic extras.
tiers.paperLevel: For a textual document set D, document clustering applies cluster analysis to obtain document groups C = {C1, ..., Ck}, where each Ci contains documents from D. Its stated applications are automatic document organization, topic extraction, and fast information retrieval or filtering.

explainer.example: A folder containing 100 textual reports is processed with cluster analysis, producing several document groups. A document system can then use those groups to organize the reports, extract topics, or support faster retrieval and filtering.

usedIn.name: Automatic document organization
usedIn.detail: Document groups provide a basis for organizing a textual collection.

usedIn.name: Topic extraction
usedIn.detail: Clustered documents can be used in extracting topics from a collection.

usedIn.name: Information retrieval
usedIn.detail: Document groups can support fast retrieval of textual information.

usedIn.name: Information filtering
usedIn.detail: Clustering can be applied to make document filtering faster.

explainer.intuition: Instead of handling a textual collection as one undivided set, use cluster analysis to produce document groups. Work with those groups when organizing documents, extracting topics, or retrieving and filtering information.
howItWorks: Start with a collection of textual documents.
Apply cluster analysis to the documents.
Obtain groups containing documents from the collection.
Use the groups for organization, topic extraction, retrieval, or filtering.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connects cluster analysis with practical ways of handling textual collections. The same document groups can support organization, topic extraction, and faster access to information.
misconceptions: Document clustering and topic extraction are not synonyms; topic extraction is one application.
It is not only a retrieval technique; document organization and filtering are also applications.
It is cluster analysis applied to textual documents, not a separate name for all clustering.

diagram.caption: Cluster analysis turns textual documents into groups used by several document-processing applications.
